sentences.text: Judgment

This judgment arise out of claim petition filed by the claimant against respondents under Section 166 of Motor Vehicles Act, 1988 (hereinafter referred as "Act") praying for awarding compensation of Rs.10,00,000/- for the injuries sustained in a road traffic accident that occurred on 09.09.2022 at about 2.30pm.

2. The case of the claimant in nutshell is that:
On 09.09.2022 at about 2.30 pm the petitioner was going towards Sarjapura side from Attibele side by riding TVS Jupiter motorcycle bearing No.KA-51- HQ-2974 on Attibele-Sarjapura road by wearing helmet.

At that time car bearing reg No.
KA-51-MP- 4746 came from opposite direction in a rash and negligent manner and dashed against the petitioner's motorcycle and caused the accident.

Due to impact,
the petitioner sustained grievous injuries.

Immediately, he was shifted to Srinivasa Speciality Hospital, treated as an inpatient by spending huge amount towards medical, hospital charges, medicines, attendant charges, conveyance, nourishing food and other incidental expenses.
Due to the said accidental injuries, he lost his income and thus suffering from permanent disability.
The injuries caused in the accident are permanent in nature.

3. It is the case of the petitioner that, Prior to accident the petitioner was hale and healthy, working as Supervisor at Kumar Organic Products Limited, Bangalore and getting salary of Rs.43,301/- per month.
The said accident occurred due to sole rash and negligent driving by the driver of the car bearing Reg.No.KA-51-MP-4746.
The respondents being the Registered owner and the insurer of the offending vehicle are jointly and severally liable to pay compensation to the petitioner.
Hence, the petitioner prayed to allow the petition and to grant compensation as prayed in the petition.
4. The respondent No.2 has appeared before this Court and filed written statement.

The respondent No.1 did not appear before this court hence, place ex-parte.
4A.

The respondent No.2 has filed the written statement denying the entire petition averments and denied the issuance of policy in favour of the 1st respondent in respect of the car bearing No.KA-51- MP-4746.
Further stated that the driver of the offending vehicle did not possess a valid driving License at the of time of accident.
There is non compliance of Sec.134(c) and 158(6) of MV Act.
It has also denied the involvement of the vehicle in the accident and rashness driving of the driver of the offending vehicle.
Further denied the age, occupation, medical expenses etc., Further contended that the compensation claimed by the petitioner is highly excessive, exorbitant.
Accordingly, the respondent No.2 prayed to dismiss the petition.

Mahaboob Khan.A vs Tushar Das on 3 September, 2025 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/42003074/
2 5.
Basing on the pleadings of the parties, the following issues are framed for determination.

Issue No.1: Whether the petitioner proves that, the accident occurred on 09-09-2022 at 2:30pm,
due to negligent driving of driver of car bearing Reg.No.KA-51-MP-4746 and in the said accident petitioner had sustained injuries?
 Issue No.2:
Whether the  petitioner is entitled for  Compensation?
If so, what is the  quantum?
From whom?
Issue No.3:- What order or Award?
6. In order to substantiate the claim petition contention, the petitioner has examined himself as PW-1 and got marked Sixteen documents as Exs.P1 to P11.
The respondent no.2 did not examine any witness nor produced any documents on its behalf.
7. The Court has heard the arguments canvassed by both sides counsel.

8. On perusal of oral and documentary evidence let in before this tribunal, my answers to the above points are as follows:
Issue No.1 :In the affirmative, Issue No.2: Partly in affirmative.
Issue No.3: As per final order, for the foregoing #REASONS#
9. Issue No.1:-
In order to substantiate the claim petition contention, the petitioner has examined himself as PW-1 and got marked Sixteen documents as Exs.P1 to P11.
The details of the exhibits are given in the annexure of the judgment.
10. It is the specific case of the respondent No.2 that the driver of the offending car did not posses a valid driving license as on the date of accident.
It has denied the involvement of the vehicle in the accident.
To prove the same it has not examined any witness nor produced any documents.
11. The petitioner has reiterated the petition averments in the chief examination.
He has duly cross examined by the counsel for respondent No.2 at length.
During the cross examination of PW.1, he has admitted his vehicle was duly insured and had DL and the complaint lodged by his brother.
He further denied other material suggestions of the counsel in the cross examination.
12. Before evaluating the evidence of the PW.1, for cost of repetition, it is necessary to reproduce the case of the petitioner.

On 09.09.2022 at about 2.30 pm the petitioner was going towards Sarjapura side from Attibele side by riding TVS Jupiter motorcycle bearing No.KA-51-HQ-2974 on Attibele-Sarjapura road by wearing helmet.
At that time car bearing reg No. KA-51-MP-4746 came from opposite direction in a rash and negligent manner and dashed against the petitioner's motorcycle and caused the accident.

Mahaboob Khan.A vs Tushar Das on 3 September, 2025 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/42003074/
3 13.
Among the documents produced, Ex.P-1 is the FIR with complaint and at Ex.P.6 is the Charge sheet
it is mentioned that the accident had occurred due to the rash and negligent driving of driver of offending car.
The police registered the case against the accused/driver of the offending vehicle for the offence punishable under section 279, 338 of Indian Penal Code.
The petitioner has produced the charge sheet at Ex.P.6.
Further it is relevant to note herein that the accused had pleaded guilty in the criminal case can be seen from Ex.P1.

The learned counsel for the insurer has vehemently argued that there is no reference of section 337 or 338 of IPC in the charge sheet and also the accused was penalized for the offense punishable under section 279 of IPC.
However, the entire documents such as police documents itself depicts that the petitioner had sustained injuries.

Hence,
mere non referring of section 337 or 338 of IPC in the charge sheet is not fatal to the case of the petitioner.

14. Thus, on an overall consideration of these documents coupled with the evidence of PW-1, it would clearly establish that the accident in question had occurred due to the negligence of the driver of the car bearing No.KA-51-MP-4746.
Therefore, I hold that the accident is caused due to sole rash and negligent driving by the driver of the car bearing reg No. KA-51-MP-4746.
The Court cannot adopt strict liability as conducted in a criminal case to prove rash and negligence on the part of the driver of the respondent vehicle.
But there should be prima-facie materials regarding rash and negligence to fix the owner and insurance company for payment of compensation.
It can be gathered in the police records that the complaint has been lodged with delay.
In the light of the Judgment in 1RAVI's case, it is manifestly clear delay in lodging the FIR cannot be the ground to deny justice to the victim.

However, the claim has to be examined with a closer scrutiny, 1 RAVI V/s.
BADRINARAYAN AND OTHERS:
(2011) 4 SCC 693 particularly the contents of the FIR
. Either First Information report and complaint does not indicates about the reasons for the delay.
But, it can be gathered that, the petitioner was not in position to lodge the complaint on the same day as he was under treatment.
There could be variety of reasons in genuine cases for delayed lodgment of FIR.
In such cases, the authenticity of the FIR assumes much more significance than delay in lodging thereof.

It is well settled position of law that the proceedings under Motor Vehicle Act are summary in nature and it is beneficial legislation and the evidence required about negligence act is sufficient if it is in the nature of preponderance of probability.
15.
The Court cannot adopt strict liability as conducted in a criminal case to prove rash and negligence on the part of the driver of the respondent vehicle.
But there should be prima-facie materials regarding rash and negligence to fix the owner and insurance company for payment of compensation.
Therefore, a straight jacket formula cannot be adopted in accepting the rash and negligence on the part of Driver of the insured.
So, the materials on record clearly indicates that the accident has occurred due to sole negligence of driver of the offending vehicle.
Hence, I answer issue No.1 in the affirmative.
16. Issue No.2: the claimant has produced OPD sheet as per Ex.P.7.
It shows that the claimant has sustained displaced fracture of left clavicle which is grievous in nature.

In this regard he has not Mahaboob Khan.A vs Tushar Das on 3 September, 2025 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/42003074/
4 examined either treated Doctor or any other doctor to assess the disability.

So, I am of the opinion that though the claimant is able to prove that he has sustained injuries in the road traffic accident but he has failed to prove that he had sustained permanent disability due to injuries sustained in the road traffic accident.

Considering the contents of OPD sheet and nature of injury sustained in the accident, it can be presumed as per Ex.P.7 that the claimant has taken treatment Srinivas Speciliaty Hospital for 1 day and he got recovered.
Apart from this the petitioner has also produced medical bills at Ex.P.8 spent towards his treatment medicines for Rs.09,046.
Therefore, these bills will not be considered to refund.
After deduction of the said bills an amount of Rs.9,046/- will be reimbursed under the head of Medical Expenses.

17. As I referred above, the petitioner had taken for 1 day, it is just and proper to award a sum of Rs.500/-per day for attendant and Rs.500/- for food and nourishment charges, which would comes Rs.1,000/-.
A sum of Rs.1,000/- is awarded under the head of attendant, food and nourishment charges.

18. Therefore, by considering the nature of injuries sustained by the claimant in the road traffic accident, nature of treatment taken by him and undergone pain and suffering during the accident and during the rehabilitation period.
Therefore, I award Rs.1,00,000/- as compensation to the claimant under the head of pain and suffering.
19. Thus, the petitioner entitled for the compensation of Rs.1,10,046/- at the at rate of 6% P.A. from the respondent No.2 as they indemnify the respondent No.1.
In view of, I answer issue No.2 in partly affirmative.
20. Issue No.3:-
In view of my findings to the above Issues, I proceed to pass the following:
ORDER The claim petition filed by claimant under section 166 of the Motor Vehicles Act, 1988 is allowed in part.

The respondent No.2 is liable to pay total compensation to the tune of Rs.1,10,046/-
(Rupees One Lakh Ten Thousand and Forty Six Only) together interest @ 6% P.A from the date of petition till realization.
The respondent No.2 is directed to deposit the said amount within 60 days from the date of this judgment after deducting any amount paid as the interim compensation.
On deposit of compensation, the petitioner is entitled to withdraw entire amount with interest as awarded amount is meager one.
The office is directed to release the entire amount to petitioner or PW.1 with interest through e- payment.
All the interim application if any pending stands disposed off.

The advocate fee of Rs.1,000/-
 fixed.
